reason: The cited evidence shows that wear can fragment oxide films (E1) and that phase-dependent corrosion occurs in eutectic HEAs (E2), but none of the passages provide direct evidence for preferential oxide disruption at phase boundaries, micro-galvanic coupling between exposed phases, or a feedback loop between wear and corrosion. The claim about homogenized microstructures forming more adherent oxides is also unsupported by the cited texts.
premises: Wear disrupts oxide films preferentially at phase boundaries due to poor adhesion from compositional heterogeneity
Exposed heterogeneous phases form micro-galvanic couples that accelerate corrosion
Galvanic corrosion prevents re-formation of a stable protective oxide
This creates a feedback loop accelerating both wear and corrosion
A homogenized microstructure forms a uniformly adherent oxide that resists disruption
